messages:
incident-bot: ALERT: High packet loss detected on egress to eu-west (AZ-b). 40% loss on prefix(s) announced via CarrierQ transit. Pager sent to @Maya Chen. Severity: P2.

Maya Chen: Ack. I'm online and taking. Starting quick blast triage — which regions are impacted?

Diego Rivera: I'm seeing replica sync timeouts and elevated 502/504 from edge->replica in eu-west. Errors started ~10:05 UTC.

Maya Chen: Confirmed 502 spikes on dashboards. Impacting cross-AZ writes for a subset of customers in eu-west. Not global.

CarrierQ NOC: carrierq-noc: We have a reported fiber degradation between FRA-IX and our downstream POP (FRA-POPA). BGP flaps observed; some paths are intermittently blackholing. Working on patch but could be multi-hour.

Samir Gupta: Can someone drop a traceroute / mtr from an affected host? Need to confirm where loss is.

Maya Chen: dropping output from a host in eu-west-azb: 
```
mtr -c 100 -r -w replica-euwb-03
Start: Wed Mar 11 10:12:15 2026
0. replica-euwb-03 (10.2.3.7) 0.2%\/0%
1. 10.2.0.1 0.0%
2. 192.0.2.5 0.0%
3. 198.51.100.1 0.4%
4. 203.0.113.9 2.2%
5. 80.11.22.33 (CarrierQ-eu) 38.0% packet loss
6. 80.11.23.1 (CarrierQ-transit) 41.0% packet loss
7. 198.51.101.5 0.0%
```
Looks like loss concentrated on CarrierQ hops.

CarrierQ NOC: Confirmed — visible loss on FRA transit pair. Engineering is isolating fiber pair and rehoming capacity. ETA unknown; we can provide temporary routing workarounds.

Lena Novak: Proposed mitigation: shift our eu-west egress to TransitY as failover via BGP communities + prepending. Can we announce more specific prefixes to prefer TransitY? Any capacity concerns?

Samir Gupta: We have spare egress capacity on TransitY for this traffic. Two quick options: 1) prepending to prefer TransitY, 2) withdraw smaller aggregates from CarrierQ and reannounce via TransitY (risk: increased route churn). Prefer 1) initially.

Maya Chen: I'll apply prepending to egress-routes for eu-west prefixes now. Rolling change: start with low-risk prefix sets (replication lanes).

Maya Chen: @oncall change command (excerpt):
```
# on BGP route-controller
announce route 203.0.113.0/24 via TransitY communities +3x-prepend
```
Applying to route-group: eu-west-replica-lanes — doing canary (5% of routers) then full.

Diego Rivera: Noted. Sync errors drop to baseline on first canary nodes within ~90s. :thumbsup:

Aisha Patel: Heads-up — I will put a "degraded performance" update on status.redwood.ai and post to customer Slack channel with a short blurb. Draft: "We are investigating higher error rates and replication delays in eu-west AZ-b due to an upstream transit provider issue. Engineers are diverting traffic; some customers may see intermittent errors."

Maya Chen: Good. Please call out replication delays for customers using cross-AZ sync.

CarrierQ NOC: We're routing around the damaged fiber and ramping alternate optical circuits. You may see transient BGP path flips in the next 20–30m. We'll notify when stable.

Samir Gupta: Handoff: I'll take on-call at 2055012700 for the next 2 hours (Maya handing off — I'm proxied). Any outstanding tasks?

Maya Chen: Handoff acknowledged. Outstanding: 1) finish full prepending rollout for all eu-west prefixes 2) coordinate with CarrierQ for final confirmation 3) monitor packet-loss dashboards for 30m post-change.

Samir Gupta: Doing full rollout now. Watching prometheus: token_loss_eu_west down from ~38% -> ~2% on most prefixes after full prepending. One prefix still showing 12% — investigating.

CarrierQ NOC: Update: we verified a damaged fiber pair, have rerouted traffic, but some microflaps remain; final repair ETA 4–6 hours.

Lena Novak: For mitigation follow-ups: schedule a post-incident review with network eng + purchasing to discuss multi-provider contracts and automatic failover playbook.

Aisha Patel: Status page updated and customer comms posted. Support triage note: escalate any customer with >5% write failure rate for dedicated follow-up.

Maya Chen: Summary for incident doc: Impact = eu-west AZ-b replication and write latency; root cause = CarrierQ fiber degradation causing BGP flaps; mitigation = BGP prepending to TransitY and CarrierQ rehoming; status = degraded -> partially mitigated (traffic redirected), repair in progress.

Samir Gupta: Will continue monitoring and will update when CarrierQ reports stable. If packet loss returns, we'll consider temporary traffic shaping at edge (drop low-priority background sync).

incident-bot: NOTE: Pager escalation suppressed (Maya handed to Samir). Incident channel archived when resolved.

Maya Chen: Thanks everyone. I'll file the incident ticket and assign postmortem owners tomorrow: Maya (ops lead), Lena (networks), Aisha (customer comms).

CarrierQ NOC: We'll post another advisory when the optical repair is complete or if ETA changes.

Samir Gupta: Closing loop for now — setting incident state to "monitoring". Will update if conditions change.
